Angry Mama vs IMPRESA: Best Microwave Steam Cleaner (2026)

$7.98 Angry Mama vs $9.99 IMPRESA 2-Pack — cleaning your microwave shouldn't require elbow grease. These steam cleaners use vinegar and water to dissolve baked-on grime in minutes. But which one wins?

Published July 20, 2026 · Based on verified Amazon product data and real customer outcomes

Cleaning a microwave is one of those kitchen chores everyone hates. The baked-on spaghetti sauce, the exploded soup, the mysterious dried-on crust that's been there since last winter — it's stubborn, sticky, and requires serious scrubbing. Or it used to. Enter the microwave steam cleaner: a simple silicone gadget that uses steam to loosen grime so you can wipe it away with a paper towel. Two of the most popular are the Angry Mama Microwave Steam Cleaner and the IMPRESA 2-Pack Microwave Steam Cleaner. Both cost under $10. Both work the same way. But one is a better value.

Quick Verdict

Buy the Angry Mama if: You want a single, well-designed steam cleaner that's easy to handle, fun to use (the angry face actually makes people smile), and works reliably every time. The locking lid prevents spills, and the compact size fits even small microwaves.

Buy the IMPRESA 2-Pack if: You have multiple microwaves (office, RV, vacation home) or want a backup. But the IMPRESA design is less refined — the lid doesn't seal as well, and the shape can be awkward to handle when hot.

Our pick: The Angry Mama Microwave Steam Cleaner. At $7.98, it's the original for a reason. Better design, better lid seal, and that iconic angry face that makes cleaning feel a little less like a chore.

Our Pick 🏆 Angry Mama Microwave Steam Cleaner

$7.98 on Amazon

The Angry Mama is the original microwave steam cleaner, and it's become something of an internet sensation. It's a small silicone vessel shaped like an angry woman's head — complete with a grouchy face and red hair that doubles as a handle. Fill it with a mixture of vinegar and water, microwave for 3-5 minutes, and the steam loosens all the dried-on food inside your microwave.

The design is surprisingly thoughtful. The locking lid has a steam-release vent that directs steam upward, and the wide base keeps it stable in the microwave. After the cycle completes, you open the microwave door and wipe the interior with a paper towel — everything comes off effortlessly, including the turntable, ceiling, and walls. The Angry Mama is made from food-grade silicone that's heat-resistant up to 450°F, and it's dishwasher safe for easy cleaning.

What makes the Angry Mama special is the attention to detail. The lid snaps shut securely — no accidental spills when carrying it to the microwave. The red "hair" handle stays cool enough to grip after the cycle. And the face, while silly, actually serves a purpose: the steam escapes through the "mouth" opening, which is angled to avoid direct contact when you open the door.

Key specs: Food-grade silicone, 3-5 min microwave cycle, vinegar + water, dishwasher safe, 4.5" tall, 3.2 oz, lid lock mechanism.

IMPRESA 2-Pack Microwave Steam Cleaner

$9.99 on Amazon

The IMPRESA Microwave Steam Cleaner 2-Pack offers a more utilitarian take on the same concept. Instead of a character design, it's a simple round silicone pod with a vented lid. You get two units for $9.99, which works out to about $5 each — cheaper than the Angry Mama on a per-unit basis.

Functionally, the IMPRESA works the same way: fill with vinegar and water, microwave for 3-5 minutes, wipe clean. The silicone construction is similar to the Angry Mama, and the size is comparable. Having two units means you can keep one at home and one at the office, or have a backup ready when one is in the dishwasher.

However, the IMPRESA has some design shortcomings. The lid doesn't seal as tightly as the Angry Mama's — several reviewers report water leaking out during the microwave cycle, which can create a mess in your microwave (defeating the purpose). The shape is also less ergonomic: it's a smooth round pod without a good gripping surface, making it tricky to handle when hot. And while the 2-pack is convenient, individual units are less durable than the Angry Mama, with some users reporting the silicone degrading after several months of use.

Key specs: Food-grade silicone, 2-pack, 3-5 min microwave cycle, dishwasher safe, simple round design, 3.5" diameter.

How They Work

Both gadgets use the same principle: heat a mixture of vinegar and water in the microwave. The steam condenses on the interior surfaces, dissolving dried-on food and grease. After 3-5 minutes, everything wipes away with a paper towel. No scrubbing, no harsh chemicals, no elbow grease. It's genuinely effective — the kind of kitchen hack that feels like cheating once you try it.

Design & Usability

The Angry Mama wins this category hands down. The locking lid is secure — no leaks during the cycle. The "hair" handle stays cool and provides a good grip. The face adds a touch of whimsy that makes cleaning less of a chore. The IMPRESA, by contrast, is purely functional. The lid doesn't seal as well, the round shape is slippery when wet, and there's no good way to handle it when it's hot out of the microwave.

Durability

The Angry Mama is made from thicker, more durable silicone. Users report it lasting for years with regular use. The IMPRESA silicone is thinner and more prone to wear, with some users reporting cracking or warping after 6-12 months. The 2-pack helps mitigate this — you have a backup when the first one wears out — but the Angry Mama's single unit will likely outlast both IMPRESA units combined.

Which Should You Buy?

The IMPRESA 2-Pack seems like the better value at first glance — $9.99 for two vs $7.98 for one. But the Angry Mama's superior design makes it the better long-term investment. A tighter lid seal means no mess during cleaning, the cool-touch handle means no burned fingers, and the thicker silicone means it'll last years instead of months. The IMPRESA works in a pinch, but the Angry Mama is the one you'll reach for week after week.

For just $7.98, the Angry Mama is one of the cheapest quality-of-life upgrades you can make for your kitchen. It turns a dreaded chore into a 5-minute no-effort task. That's worth the price of admission alone.

🧪 Recipe: Fill to the fill line with white vinegar (or use 50/50 vinegar and water). Microwave on high for 3 minutes. Let it sit for 2 minutes (don't open the door). Then wipe everything clean. For tough stains, add a squeeze of lemon juice.
